💡 Key Takeaways

  • Cobb called it an “out of body experience” watching her scenes come to life, adding, “So that was really really cool because that was Sophie’s initiation into this world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hunting Wives author May Cobb is addressing the show’s deviation from the book ahead of the highly-anticipated season 2.

“I feel like [creator] Rebecca [Cutter] did such a great job of keeping the spirit of the book — the unhinged spirit — very much intact,” Cobb exclusively told Us. “The first scene that I got to see them film was the skeet shooting scene — and that scene to me in the book was near and dear to my heart. So I was so happy that it stayed and it was the first one I got to see.”.

Cobb called it an “out of body experience” watching her scenes come to life, adding, “So that was really really cool because that was Sophie’s initiation into this world. That’s the moment where she’s going to cross over and decide to descend with the hunting wives.”.

Recent findings suggest that based on Cobb’s book of the same name, The Hunting Wives introduced Sophie (Brittany Snow), who moved from Boston to an East Texas town where she found herself drawn to prominent socialite Margo (Malin Åkerman). While some became invested in the murder at the center of the series, The Hunting Wives also provided plenty of entertainment with guns, drinking and steamy onscreen hookups.

“Rebecca told me when we first met that she was going to change up the ending to where Margo lives. My response to her was, ‘Where were you when I was writing this book? That’s so much better,'” Cobb recalled. “So I was so happy with that, I was just so happy with all the story they added — making Dermot Mulroney’s character Jed a fully-fleshed character. He really didn’t have much of a presence in the book and then now he’s running for governor and I thought that was such a cool story line. I thought that was also genius.”.

According to an official synopsis, season 2 of The Hunting Wives picks up with Sophie and Margo “on the outs.”.

“Rebecca, the writers, the cast and just everyone involved creatively have turned a show that was already at an 11 and dialed it up even more exponentially,” Cobb teased. “There are higher stakes. It’s just wild.”.

In addition to The Hunting Wives returning on Thursday, November 26, Cobb is continuing to expand her book universe with a sequel to All the Little Houses — which is also about to be brought to life on screen.

“When I was writing All the Little Houses, I got almost almost halfway through when I realized I had way too much for one book — and way way too much drama — so I knew that I needed to make it a series,” Cobb exclusively told Us about All the Little Secrets, which is out now.

In a recent development, cobb was thrilled to return to Longview, Texas, in the sequel but she isn’t sure about another continuation — yet, adding, “I would love to keep that open as a possibility. Right now, we don’t have looks for a book 3 for this. It is a duology, but never say never.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The thing you must understand is that I'm not mad. No, really, I'm not upset at all—as a matter of fact, I'm happy for your level 60 character to complete Scarlet Subterfuge (and its follow-up, In Dreams) with less back-and-forth trekking than me. I'm chuffed for you. Really, I am.

Ahem—as you can tell by my current state of grumpiness, WoW: Forever issued a bunch of hotfixes, which I will do my due diligence in describing before I have a good moan: Alterac Valley has had some tweaks to stop people "frequently completing the battleground without capturing the objectives", balance druids have had some buffs, and some major bugs (such as hunter pets not being able to crit) have been addressed.

That last point's a bit of contention in the community, given hunters are out-performing other classes in damage, but given we're just three weeks into the game with a couple of weeks left to go before the raid tier, I'm not sweating the lack of an immediate nerf bat.

According to recent reports, right, there's my journalistic obligation taken care of. Here's why I'm (not) upset.

Scarlet Subterfuge—and In Dreams—is widely considered one of the crappiest quests in Classic, and given this is a game that's already rife with inconvenience—inconvenience I am usually all for—that's saying something. In it, you need to go and find Highlord Taelan Fordring, son of Tirion Fordring, and remove the scarlet-coloured wool from his eyes.

Industry observers note that story-wise, this quest kicks ass. You're finding the son of the guy who wielded the Ashbringer. Realising his life has been a lie, he hulks out, cleaving down his former scarlet allies, and marches out of the fortress side-by-side with you. Mechanically, it sucks so much, dude.

According to recent reports, to reach Fordring the younger, you need to go halfway across the zone, talk to an illusionist hermit, and don a disguise. Then you need to jog all the way up to where Taelan is to give him the news.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The only downside is that this disguise lasts for 30 minutes, and escorting Taelan, at least with the current strategy (more on this later) lasts for about 20 minutes. And if you don't have the disguise on, he's hostile to you, even if you're just restarting the escort quest. So that means that if anybody else is doing the quest by the time you get there, you need to either:.

The actual escort is annoying, too: Since Taelan can technically handle the Scarlet Crusade on his lonesome, accepted practice for this quest has been to simply let him handle things. Which both makes it take ages and makes it difficult to find a group so that you can do it the intended way.

Recent findings suggest that as a cherry on top, you can't really skip this quest outright as it gives some really powerful pre-BiS endgame items. Still, I persevered, I did it yesterday, and Blizzard, uh. Blizzard gave the disguise an hour-long duration literally today.

"Western Plaguelands - The Scarlet Illusion granted during the quest 'Scarlet Subterfuge' now lasts an hour (was 30 minutes).".

It has been revealed that this doesn't make the quest any less of a headache to finish, but hey—at least if someone else is already doing it, you won't have to jog back to your hag friend or play the log-in, log-out Hokey Pokey until he respawns. Good for you.

In a recent development, the United Video Game Workers-CWA union has released a report with details on the hardship fund it started in collaboration with Necrosoft Games earlier this year benefiting laid-off developers. The UVW reports that through its itch.io bundle and from monies received via union dues and outside donations, it raised $290,000 over two weeks. All that cash has been dispersed to over 150 devs from across the industry to help with expenses like rent, medical bills, and other debt.

"This came at a time when I deeply, deeply needed a hand to pull me up while I'm drowning.".

Thanks to your support, we were able to disburse $290K in funds to over 150 game workers facing hardship after unprecedented mass layoffs.

Perusing the report’s list of studios from which applicants to the fund have been laid off is depressing. Among them are some of the biggest names in the industry: Xbox, Activision Blizzard, EA, Ubisoft, and more. It’s the human reckoning, the terrible price to all the industry upheaval that’s often glossed over in reports on resets, booming financials, and robust pipelines. The other equally sad detail is just how long many of these out-of-work people have worked in the industry, with 32 percent of applicants reporting 10 years or more.

According to recent reports, the industry is experiencing a brain drain that will be incredibly difficult to recover from. Nintendo is able to make the games it can because it retains its employees, training them up to eventually lead games of their own. Jason Schreier reported at Bloomberg that 21 percent of Rockstar staff are vets with 10-plus years of experience, and they’ve just released what has the potential to be the best-selling, best-reviewed game of all time.

It has been revealed that here is a remarkable stat: Rockstar told me that 21% of their employees, or around 1,000 people, have been at the firm for 10+ years. As game companies everywhere lay off tens of thousands of staff, the biggest hit of the year came from a team full of veterans www.bloomberg.com/news/newslet….

In a recent development, this fund has helped people in need keep their homes and bridge the gap between former employment and new jobs. The UVW claims it hopes to run fundraisers like this in the future as it continues to fight for worker protections and organize new studios.

In addition to a five-days-a-week in-office mandate, the firm is also offering employee buyouts.

The union has spent over two years trying to negotiate its first contract.

GTA 6 reportedly sets massive livestreaming record, watched more in its first week than Elden Ring, Diablo 4, Valorant, and Lost Ark combined

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has broken another livestreaming record.
  • It has been revealed that over its first seven days on sale, GTA 6 has amassed over 420m hours watched, according to Streams Charts.
  • Sources indicate that as for the livestreaming platforms that saw the largest audiences for GTA 6, YouTube reportedly had the lead in average audience numbers during the first six hours of launch, but Twitch took over in content volume in the days that followed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has broken another livestreaming record. After attracting more viewers across livestreaming platforms than any game ever on its launch day, Rockstar's open-world crime sim has reportedly continued to dominate on platforms like Twitch, YouTube, and Kick.

It has been revealed that over its first seven days on sale, GTA 6 has amassed over 420m hours watched, according to Streams Charts. That's nearly three times more than the previous record, held by Valorant's closed beta in April 2020. In fact, that 420m hours tally is more than the first-week watch time achieved by Valorant, Elden Ring, Diablo 4, and Lost Ark combined.

Sources indicate that as for the livestreaming platforms that saw the largest audiences for GTA 6, YouTube reportedly had the lead in average audience numbers during the first six hours of launch, but Twitch took over in content volume in the days that followed. In fact, Twitch's GTA 6 watch time was higher at launch than any other game in its history.

In a recent development, streams Charts also noted 1,056 channels reached new all-time peak viewership numbers while streaming GTA 6, in some cases multiplying their previous record tenfold. Major content creators like IShowSpeed, IlloJuan, and TheBurntPeanut stole the spotlight, but GTA 6 also helped many other channels set new viewership records.

Recent findings suggest that livestreaming, of course, isn't the only area where GTA 6 has set new records. Publisher Take-Two called it the biggest entertainment launch in history, generating $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue from 32.5m copies sold on day one. Other parts of the industry have benefited, too. Anticipation for GTA 6 boosted US hardware sales for both PlayStation and Xbox, just as GTA 6 became each console brand's most pre-ordered title ever. At launch, more than 39 million people played GTA 6 on PS5, according to Sony. The game also had the highest number of concurrent players ever on any PlayStation console, beating even the most popular free-to-play titles.

Recent findings suggest that you can check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough if you're in need of assistance, which we just updated today with a guide on how to whistle in GTA 6 - something I didn't know you could do. The walkthrough also covers other lesser-known mechanics such as how to steal ATMs in GTA 6, and much more besides.

Bringing Austen, Wharton, and Steinbeck Into the iPhone Age

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means.
  • It has been revealed that “You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone?
  • “So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” says Frost, as understanding dawns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means. Frost has never heard the term; her fellow showrunners Alderton and Zoe Kazan have.

It has been revealed that “You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone? It looks like it’s seen a lute and a loom,” Alderton tells Frost.

“So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” says Frost, as understanding dawns. Alderton and Kazan affirm her: “Yes, yes. Exactly.”.

Now that Frost gets it, she turns back to the group’s Zoom screen. “Sorry, what was the question?”.

Kazan began her career as an actor, while Alderton started out as a dating columnist and Frost was a sculptor and painter. Now all three are overseeing vastly different but comparable Netflix period dramas, each based on a classic work of literature: East of Eden (Kazan’s, which was released October 1), Pride and Prejudice (Alderton’s, out December 3), and The Age of Innocence (Frost’s, coming February 18). They’ve gathered in a London conference room at Netflix headquarters for a roundtable discussion about art, work, the unique experience of adapting a beloved book—and, apparently, iPhone face.

Recent findings suggest that though this is the first time the trio has met face to face, their conversation flows so easily and naturally that interrupting them with questions sometimes feels impolite. Early on, I note that all three of these novels are, on some level, about unconventional women. Alderton, Frost, and Kazan pause for a moment, considering this Lit 101–level observation.

“That’s true, I think,” agrees Frost.

And then they’re off to more interesting topics.

Vanity Fair: Have you read each other’s books?

Dolly Alderton: No, I haven’t read either of your books.

Alderton: Did you read them at school, or did you read them for fun?

According to recent reports, frost: Pride and Prejudice I read when I was a teenager at school. East of Eden I read first about 15 years ago, I think.

Alderton: So Em already wins the round table.

Frost: And for both of you, was it the thing you most wanted to adapt?

In a recent development, alderton: I would never have dared to dream to. I was so overwhelmed when I was first approached. I just thought, it’s such a precious IP. It would be way too much, and I wouldn’t be the right person. But then when I was asked to pitch for it, at that point there’s no other answer but yes.

Kazan: First of all, was it the Austen you liked the most?

Alderton: Yes. It was the one that I’ve always loved because of Lizzie Bennet. I’ve always been obsessed with Lizzie Bennet. She was my hook. But how about you two? Did you ever dream of adapting these texts?

Frost: I was at a place where I said, “I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period.” Netflix asked me to do The Age of Innocence, and it was, I think at that moment, the one book that made me just go, “Oh my God, okay, let me go back and revisit it.” Because I know I love it, but you have to know what the reason is [to adapt it again]. And the thing that totally blew me away on a reread was how relevant and resonant it is. It is about the freedom of the individual versus the conformity of the pack. It has so many themes in it that are really resonant with social media, the bullying of the group.

Industry observers note that alderton [turning to Kazan]: Tackling Cathy, how did you begin? What was your way into that?

In a recent development, kazan: I think of adaptation as an advanced form of reading. For me, everything I’ve ever written has come from a feeling of “I have to write this specific thing.” When I was 15 and I read the book for the first time, I felt like it literally grabbed me by the throat and wouldn’t let go. And then I just kept coming back to it. And specifically her character, I felt like I had never read anyone like that before or since.

[to Alderton] The BBC’s Pride and Prejudice—is that the one that you—.

Alderton: No, that wasn’t my Pride and Prejudice.

Industry observers note that alderton: Yeah, the Joe Wright one was the one that I was more familiar with. But I’m so interested in what you were saying about getting to know Cathy. I was kind of nervous about doing press for a book that’s so beloved, and I’m finding it’s actually been really easy so far because I just know the people so well. So much of it has been basically like, putting Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth, all the Bennet family and Bingley through therapy. That psychological interrogation of these very well-known characters has been the thing I’ve just really, really enjoyed.

Industry observers note that frost: Have you both had to change points of view from the novel? Do you feel like you’ve had to make a specific choice about who you are foregrounding? I think I know the answer in your case, Zoe.

Kazan: No, I actually don’t. I’m aware that the way that I read a book is different from the way that anyone else reads that book. When I read East of Eden, I feel like I see Steinbeck becoming enthralled by this character, finding her as curious as I do. I think he starts out a real place of judgment and over the course of the book, really moves towards love and understanding.

Sources indicate that alderton: I have a similar thing in that for the majority of the book, one of the lead characters is completely unknowable. Not just to Elizabeth, but to the audience as well. So you have to honor that to make it satisfying. That’s kind of frustrating when you’re writing a romantic lead for the first three and a half episodes. None of us, least of all the female protagonist, can see who he is, and we misunderstand him. There is no other option I think than staying with Lizzie.

Recent findings suggest that frost: It’s very different because the book is entirely from Newland’s point of view. The thing that I wanted to do, and that Netflix were really excited for me to do, was to open it up to find out who the women were.

Recent findings suggest that I think in the book—rightly, because she’s writing from Newland’s point of view—both May and Ellen are sort of constructed as his other. One is the thing to be won, and one is effectively the antagonist. It’s so interesting, because it’s a female author—and [Wharton herself], she’s part Newland. That's who she was growing up. And she’s part Ellen, this woman who now lives in Europe, who's become really cosmopolitan, who is even based on her own love triangle.

The impossibility of that love triangle is the thing I want people to feel. It’s not like one of them is wrong. They're all just feeling what they’re feeling.

Sources indicate that alderton: And how do you feel about bringing that latest perspective and analysis to the story? For a book that's so beloved, did you feel excited by that? Or did you feel kind of daunted by it?

Frost: Maybe I should have felt daunted. I didn’t. I think Edith Wharton—it’s so based on her own personal experience of when she was 45, she had this sexual awakening. She was in this really dull marriage. She’d never had an orgasm. When she was 45, she fell in love with this journalist and had this passionate affair.

Recent findings suggest that frost: She had this big affair, then he ghosted her. But she was trying to make sense of it through this love triangle. When she wrote it, she couldn’t possibly have written herself as a female character in the center of an illicit love triangle because we were still in time of censorship, and she was being published in a very commercial magazine. So she had to make herself the man that has more agency.

Recent findings suggest that alderton: With any script, you have a relationship with the characters. But with what we are doing, you have this relationship with the writer.

Sources indicate that kazan to Alderton: You’re also a novelist. How are you thinking about bisecting yourself—using both parts of your brain, the novelist part and the dramatist part?

Alderton: I’ll tell you how I felt about it. I’ve written two novels, both of which I’ve tried to adapt. I found it really, really hard. I found adapting Pride and Prejudice incredibly effortless. When I went from Pride and Prejudice to my novel, I was like, "Why is this so much harder? I hate this novelist. Jane Austen is so much easier.".

What amazed me is just, it’s like she wrote it to be adapted. It’s like her agent had said to her, “I know you’re going to write this novel about this family of five women, but remember, we could get a great movie deal off the back of it. So try and make it as adaptable as possible.” It has literally been written for TV in this totally perfect six-part structure. I just wish she was around to have written screenplays.

In a recent development, kazan: This is how I feel about Tolstoy too. When I read War and Peace, I’m like, “Oh, he’s seeing it as if it’s a movie.” It’s very strange to read that so far ahead of the technology to make that possible.

According to recent reports, where was each of your point of entry? What was the first scene that you wrote?

Frost: I always break the whole thing in quite a lot of detail to feel like I understand where the story's going. I think when I actually started writing, I probably wrote from the beginning.

Kazan: So you outlined her therapy?

Sources indicate that alderton: I do the same. It’s the only thing that gives me freedom and confidence to write.

Kazan: And did you know how many episodes you wanted from the start, or did that change?

Frost: At one point it was longer, and at one point it was shorter. It’s eight in the end. What about you?

Industry observers note that kazan: I wanted eight originally, and then for budget and logistical reasons, I had to boil it down to seven quite late in the process. I had been four years into adapting it.

In a recent development, kazan: Yeah. And we were a month away from production, and I had to restructure everything quite late in the game.

It has been revealed that kazan: Yeah, but you know what? It was actually this enormous gift. I had this writing teacher in college, a poetry teacher who talked a lot about constraints. And I don’t know if you've ever seen the... What’s his name? He’s a nightmare, but forgive me—the guy who directed Melancholia.

Industry observers note that kazan: There’s this beautiful Lars Von Trier film called The Five Obstructions, a documentary. He challenges his filmmaking teacher to remake this perfect short film that he made in the 1960s with five sets of obstructions to help him break open his creative process again. And that, combined with what my poetry teacher was always saying—which is the form gives you freedom.

Industry observers note that kazan: I feel like having to... Every time I’ve received, “Okay, we don’t have the money for X, or we don’t have the location for Y, or you have to boil eight episodes down to seven,” that it made me think again about, okay, what’s important here? Seeing the instruction as a gift rather than as an obstacle really just helped me over and over again. I actually gave myself one night to be really mad about it, and then the next day I was—.

Industry observers note that kazan: A lot of showrunning, for me at least, has been about learning how to manage my emotions on my own time so that I can go to work and help manage everything. The next day, as soon as I started reworking it, I discovered all of the gifts that it would give me.

Recent findings suggest that alderton: That lesson is one that you only learn with the privilege of experience. This is only my second TV show. My first, Everything I Know About Love, was an adaptation of my memoir. But I remember now the moments where I remarked, “If we have to lose this scene, there’s no point shooting the whole show.” Things like that.

Kazan: And then you’re in the edit and you’re like, “Actually, that’s better.”.

According to recent reports, alderton: Totally. Or I think back on these things that we couldn’t afford or practically couldn’t work that I really thought would rip out the heart and soul of the show. And now I never dream of an alternate version of that show where those things were put in.

I don’t think I would’ve been as zen as you. I think I would’ve been a petty, grouchy bitch for three days, rather than one.

Industry observers note that kazan: At that point, I was still trying to get my greenlight. I want to hear Dolly’s answer to the first scene question.

According to recent reports, alderton: Oh, sure. So the opening of Pride and Prejudice in the book is obviously setting up the central drama, which is “we need a man. There's a latest man in town.” We decided to put Darcy at the very, very top of the show. There is so much in Pride and Prejudice to delight in. What is easy to forget is that it is the best love story of all time. And I’m just like, “We should land that. The first thing we should land is this intrigue between these two characters.”.

Industry observers note that so Elizabeth is walking around Netherfield Park being kind of nosy and breaking the rules, and she’s intrigued by this man. So much of their attraction to each other, which everyone finds so delicious to read, is that they’re just fascinated with each other, and it takes them a while to work out why. So we wanted to establish that.

Kazan: I love that. I loved her spying and the sort of misunderstanding of who he is.

Dolly, were you wrestling at all about what to do with “it’s truth universally acknowledged,” the most famous line in literature?

Recent findings suggest that alderton: Andrew Davies gives that line to Elizabeth Bennet, but for me, it felt like it’s the Mrs. Bennet line. The reinterpretation, I suppose, that I’ve done on my Pride and Prejudice is a bit of a justice for Mrs. Bennet. I’m working so hard in this adaptation to really understand why she is the way she is, why she’s so hysterical, why she's seemingly such a social climber. So to give her that line, it felt like we were just off to the races. This is a woman whose preoccupation in life is making sure her daughters are safe. So yeah, it felt like it was an easy line for Olivia [Colman].

When it comes to casting, can you articulate what makes somebody feel appropriate for a period show, versus somebody who seems too contemporary?

Kazan: Or maybe that’s not a concern.

It has been revealed that frost: I think for me, casting is really instinctive. Ben Radcliffe, right from his first tape, I was just, “He is Newland Archer. That is the end of the conversation. We are having him.”.

Kazan: Did you audition all of them?

Recent findings suggest that frost: All of them did tapes or auditions. It’s so hard to explain, isn’t it? You see somebody and you just go, “That’s what I have in my head. That’s what we need.”.

Alderton: We kind of knew who we wanted Lizzie and Darcy to be, and we had to do chemistry. We did a chemistry [read] with Emma and Jack, and Emma’s an EP on the show. So the minute Jack left, Emma and I looked at each other, and we were like, “That’s totally Darcy.”.

Sources indicate that but it’s interesting that you were saying that thing about chemistry. I don’t know about you guys, but every time I do casting, I’m amazed how much it feels like falling in love. You go away and you find yourself Googling them and thinking about them and dreaming about them. It’s so wonderful if then they want to do it, and it’s so heartbreaking if they don’t.

Kazan: You fall in love, and then sometimes your love affair doesn’t work out.

Alderton: What was your process like?

Frost: Florence [Pugh] was involved really early, right?

According to recent reports, kazan: She was. I had always had this feeling about East of Eden, and I had sort of tried to ignore that feeling because of my grandfather’s relationship to the material and my relationship to coming from this family. And about a year and a half before this call came, I had written my agent saying, “This is so embarrassing, but if the rights to East of Eden ever come up, can you please let me know so that I can pitch on it?” So they did me a solid. I got an appointment to meet, but I didn’t have a lot of time to prepare.

They asked, “Do you have any actors in mind?” I think I had walked into the room not thinking that I had any actors in mind, and then Florence came out of my mouth. I had seen Midsommar, and I felt like I was witnessing the birth of a genius. And Cathy Ames is such a challenging part that I needed an actor of that caliber. But then we didn’t do any more casting for four years after that.

Frost: But she stayed faithful.

Kazan: She did. The whole reason this show came together when it did was that there was a window that she had in her schedule. We didn’t have directors yet, and we didn’t have any other cast yet. Her window was starting in October, and between April and June, we put everything together.

So much of it is alchemical. But once you have that central pole that all the spokes are going to come off of, then you start going, “Okay, well if it’s this Lizzie Bennet, it has to be that Mr. Darcy. If it’s this Newland Archer, it has to be this Ellen.”.

It has been revealed that on the page, East of Eden is the only one of these three novels that has a protagonist who isn’t white. But that isn’t true of your series. I’m curious, Emma and Dolly, if you can speak to that—casting actors who aren’t white in these stories that are largely about white characters.

Frost: Yeah. Edith Wharton came from such a privileged, elite white bubble. That is completely what her life was. But the story is about a man who is chafing against that, and these rules are killing him. So having the contrast of the world inside and outside of that elite white bubble felt crucial to telling this story. And Ellen is part of this really exciting wave of immigration that’s coming into New York at the time, and it’s blowing this old world to pieces. And it’s so much more exciting than this kind of decaying, crusty world that he’s been trapped by.

Sources indicate that so for me, it felt like a very organic thing to have non-white characters as well that provide that contrast. They are the new ideas, they are the exciting conversations, they are the music that’s coming in. So he was one foot in each, and it was a very organic thing to do.

Alderton: I think there are so many different ways that you can look at diversity with period work. Bridgerton’s a great example of a specific thing. Colorblind casting is a specific example. We decided that we wanted our Pride and Prejudice to be very rooted in historical reality, but we also didn’t want to make an all-white Pride and Prejudice. We wanted to be inclusive and representative. So we just did our homework, and we found cases of families much like the Bingleys who had roots in trade where there were mixed-race families.

It has been revealed that was it the most common thing in Regency England? No. But it’s not the most common thing that a man like Mr. Darcy would’ve married Elizabeth Bennet. It’s so simple in my mind. It’s all made up anyway, and those actors were the best actors for those roles.

According to recent reports, kazan: Can I also say—we have white-presenting actors in East of Eden who have Caribbean roots, and Chinese American people that present as white in our series. I think the idea of whiteness, it can be a weapon. I think it can be weaponized: who we say is white and who we say isn’t white. I just think it’s a funny thing of who we agree is allowed to be in these things and who isn’t.

I do always think it’s a hard thing, because racial identity is such an notable part of how people go through the world. And what both of you are saying about finding the logic within your stories for the casting that you want to make, I think, is really important. But I also think it's important to think about how there are identities that are not visible.

Was there one moment from each of your novels that you were the most nervous about getting right?

According to recent reports, frost: I don’t know if it’s one piece of the novel per se, but what gave me pause was trying to find a way into Ellen, Countess Olenska. I wanted to find a way to stay completely true to the spirit and intention of her as a character, but make her emotionally legible to a 21st-century audience. As framed in the novel, there is an element of her being beaten by her husband, and now she needs another man to rescue her. That isn’t this sort of independent, forward-looking woman that I felt I needed at the center of the show.

Industry observers note that but Edith Wharton, as ever, is so brilliant that she sort of provided this solution partly through me drawing on her own life, which I used to infuse Ellen. Also, without giving spoilers, there are things that are said about Ellen in the novel that Ellen never confirms. We are in a world of rumor and reputation, and it suddenly became clear to me that what is said about her isn't necessarily true. Once I felt I understood who she was, the whole thing just sort of opened up for me. What about you guys?

Alderton: My take is not so much because of the text—it was because of a previous adaptation.

Kazan: I was going to ask you guys about this.

Alderton: About these adaptations that live in your head.

Kazan: All three of these books have multiple—if not multiple, at least a beloved adaptation.

Alderton: Totally. And on the whole, I feel very comfortable being in this great tradition of every 20 or 30 years, there's a Pride and Prejudice. I like that. I don't want to pretend like there are no other adaptations.

Sources indicate that but the one thing that was in my head from the very beginning was the wet-shirt moment. Because it’s such a pivotal moment in the story when we see Darcy for who he is the first time. We understand why he’s been so guarded. We understand why he grips to these social structures so strongly. We understand that he’s a deeply honorable, protective, very recently wounded man.

Saved By the Bell alum Tiffani Thiessen is offering fans a candid patch on her upcoming hip replacement surgery.

“As of right now, I am not getting it because of just the timing of travel, and I start season 2 very soon, so I’m looking at doing it next year after I finish season 2 of my show,” Thiessen, 52, said while speaking to Woman’s World in an interview published on Wednesday, November 25, referring to her Disney+ show Coven Academy.

“So right now, it’s kind of steroid shots to kind of help me through — which, my last one I just got last week helped tremendously,” she continued. “I even played pickleball for four hours and didn’t feel a thing, so we’re good.”.

She added of her future surgery, “It is definitely something in my very near future that I need to get done. And that’s okay. It’s part of it, right? Part of getting old and being active.”.

The actress revealed on a November 10 episode Tom Papa’s eponymous podcast that she needs to undergo a surgical hip replacement after learning she had “hip dysplasia” while seeking a second medical opinion.

It has been revealed that “I have to get a hip replacement — I do,” she revealed at the time. “I was a dancer when I was younger, which was a good thing, [and] I have a torn labrum, that’s one matter I have. Then, I found out, going to my second opinion, … I have hip dysplasia.”.

Hip dysplasia, according to the Cleveland Clinic, occurs when bones in the hip joint no longer properly fit together.

“So, when I was very flexible as a young child has now caused my concern now,” she continued. “I hear the hip replacements aren’t as bad as knee and shoulders [replacement procedures].”.

According to Theissen, she was in so much pain at the time that she was unable to carry out certain tasks, including a friendly game of pickleball — an matter that, according to the actress, have since been remedied thanks to the shots she’s receiving until she can go under the knife.

According to recent reports, “We play [as a family],” the actress, who shares two kids with husband Brady Smith, added at the time. “My doctor didn’t say it was pickleball, but it probably is not help[ful]. I have not been able to play in the last couple weeks ‘cause my hip’s been so bad.”.

On Wednesday, Thiessen opened up about the pain she was feeling prior to her diagnosis and discovering her health issue would require surgery.

“I was having a lot of pain in my hip, and I was… my mobility had changed on the one side of my left hip,” she explained. “When you’re born with really shallow hips, being very athletic and like a dancer and a runner and all those things that I was, I have just worn down my hips so much that because I don’t have a ton of coverage, it just makes it 10 times worse.”.

She added, “So, that’s what’s caused a lot of the pain that I’ve been in. That’s what a newly introduced hip’s gonna give me, new life again, so we’ll get there. I’m gonna thrive next year. Who knows, maybe I’ll do another marathon.”.

The Pros sound great, come with excellent noise cancellation and transparency modes, and are packed with modern features that go beyond listening to music. I'd recommend these to any Apple user looking for the best overall audio experience at full price, but when they're $100 off, I actively encourage you to buy these now.

In a recent development, on the surface, Apple's third-generation AirPods Pro are among the best ways to listen to audio on your Apple devices. The earbuds sound great: I'm not an audiophile or a headphone reviewer, but to my ears, the Pros deliver excellent sound quality, with plenty of bass and great sound separation. I frequently turn to mine when I want to pay close attention to a newly introduced album, or watch a show or movie with intricate sound design. Plus, like other AirPods, the Pros are great for jumping between your various Apple devices. I'm constantly switching between my iPhone, Mac, and Apple TV with mine, and they seamlessly move between each—at least, most of the time.

According to recent reports, the noise cancellation on these AirPods is also stellar. I used to take my AirPods Max with me on planes, but lately, I've been fine with just my Pros, since the noise cancellation seemingly blocks just about as much background sound as my over-the-ear headphones. Equally great are both the transparency modes, which pump in outside sounds while you're wearing your AirPods, and Adaptive Transparency, which automatically adjusts the level of transparency based on how loud or soft your surroundings are. This is a great mode for wearing your AirPods in loud environments, so you can still hear everything without the noise becoming overwhelming. To that point, these AirPods are actually FDA-certified hearing aids.

Sources indicate that there are plenty of other features available here as well, especially if you have a compatible iPhone. AirPods Pro 3 have a built-in heart rate sensor, so you can track workouts without an Apple Watch; you can translate conversations in real time with Live Translate; "Conversation Awareness" lowers the volume of your audio and turns on transparency mode when you start speaking; and they run for eight hours on one charge with noise cancellation enabled.

Sources indicate that this isn't an in-depth list of the AirPods Pro 3's set of features. But suffice it to say, these earbuds are worth their full MSRP of $249. So not only can I wholeheartedly recommend them at $149, but I'd say they're an easy buy if you've been thinking about picking up AirPods for yourself.

There's A Reason Ross Isn’t In One Of The Biggest Friends Scenes (But It Did Lead To A Good Joke)

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Given that the core premise of Friends centered on the friendships between Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler and Joey, it makes sense that many of the iconic sitcom's biggest moments would feature all six characters together.
  • According to recent reports, the end of Season 6 of Friends was a significant one.
  • Recent findings suggest that monica and Chandler's romantic engagement scene is topped off by Joey, Phoebe and Rachel coming in to celebrate with them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Given that the core premise of Friends centered on the friendships between Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler and Joey, it makes sense that many of the iconic sitcom's biggest moments would feature all six characters together. However, there was one huge event that didn't include David Schwimmer's character, and there's a specific reason why. While Ross's absence from this particular scene was unfortunate, it did lead to a clever joke and a nod to something the character had become notorious for.

According to recent reports, the end of Season 6 of Friends was a significant one. Chandler had done too good a job throwing Monica off the scent of his planned proposal – so much so that it seemed like she was actually considering Richard's proposal of marriage and a family – and was frantic to correct the situation. The big twist came when he came rushing back to the apartment, being made to believe he was too late, only to find Monica waiting for him with a proposal of her own.

Recent findings suggest that monica and Chandler's romantic engagement scene is topped off by Joey, Phoebe and Rachel coming in to celebrate with them. The only person absent was Ross. No, David Schwimmer and Friends weren't "on a break," he was just busy overseas when the engagement scene was filmed.

It has been revealed that as Friends co-creator David Crane pointed out on the DVD commentary, all of David Schwimmer's scenes for the two-part Season 6 finale had to be filmed in the first week because the actor was in England filming Band of Brothers for HBO. Crane spoke about having to film the scene without Schwimmer, saying:.

It has been revealed that it was frustrating not having him because you feel as though there's a major event on the show, Monica and Chandler are engaged, and all the friends run in, but not quite all the friends. The moment still works, and it's still moving, but it would have been nice to have him for that, but we were not prepared to film that scene the previous week.

While all of the drama between Monica and Chandler was going on throughout "The One with the Proposal," Ross was busy breaking up with college student Elizabeth (a cliffhanger involving her revealing she's pregnant was discussed for the season finale, but ultimately scrapped). From what it sounds like, that was all filmed during the first week of production for these final episodes. The grand finale involving Chandler and Monica wasn't filmed until later.

As you'll recall, as the gang is celebrating with a group hug, Phoebe points out that "Ross isn't here!" to which Rachel responds, "Oh, hell, he's done this three times. He knows what it's about!" It's a funny way to acknowledge and then dismiss Ross's absence from his sister and best friend's engagement, while also firing a shot at Ross's "three-divorce guy" reputation. As Crane put it, that was the silver lining to the situation, after debating whether or not to point out the lack of Ross in the scene:.

According to recent reports, there was a lot of debate. Do you need to acknowledge the fact that Ross isn't here? Or do you just let it go? And it actually gave us a really good joke.

In a recent development, I'll admit, the absence of a main character due to the actor being involved in another project might bother me under other circumstances, but it's hard to complain here. Band of Brothers is its own kind of epic, after all. Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks' HBO miniseries – based on Stephen Ambrose's non-fiction book about a parachute infantry tech giant serving in World War II – won several Emmys and has been widely remembered and appreciated in the decades since its release. What's more, Schwimmer's portrayal of Captain Herbert Sobel is easily one of his most memorable roles outside of the hit sitcom.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

The writers made the best of the situation by working in the joke about marriage proposals being old hat for Ross.

It has been revealed that ultimately, Ross did get in on the celebrations for Monica and Chandler, but it doesn't happen until the start of the following season. Ross learns about his sister and Chandler's engagement early in the Season 7 premiere, when he indicates up at the apartment with a bottle of champagne and a candy bar that they requested him to bring.

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rob NelsonRockstar Games.

Grand Theft Auto 6Â contains a surprising but cool cameo hidden near the very end of the game’s main story. So when I got a chance to chat with Rockstar’s head of production, Rob Nelson, about GTA 6 ahead of the game’s launch, I had to ask about this moment, how it came about, and what it means for the character.

It has been revealed that but uh… major spoilers. Seriously, if you’re a big GTA nerd and love to be surprised, turn around right now and stop reading. You’ll thank me later when you reach this point and get to experience it unspoiled. For those who don’t care or who can’t resist the siren’s call of secrets being revealed, keep scrolling past the warning. Just don’t yell at me later!

Recent findings suggest that as you approach the final missions in the game, Jason and Lucia start working with Giorgio, a very rich shipping magnate who works with Eastern European criminals to smuggle drugs across the ocean on his big ships. And things aren’t going well, forcing Giorgio to work with Jason, Lucia, and others on a big, ambitious plan to steal back all the cocaine confiscated by the Coast Guard as part of a large heist. But before they can pull off the heist, a higher-up from the big Balkan cartel Giorgio has been working with arrives to kill him for screwing up, but gives him one more chance to get back the coke. That badass hitman? Niko Bellic, the playable protagonist of 2008’s Grand Theft Auto IV.

Here’s the scene from GTA 6 in which he appears:.

According to recent reports, I asked Nelson if they’d planned to include Niko from the start, and he tells me that they hadn’t. Instead, he told me that the cameo came about “very organically.”.

Mike McCarthy has broken his silence after Aaron Rodgers was shockingly cut from the team after he publicly slammed the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach.

“It was a process that went on throughout this week,” McCarthy, 63, told reporters on Wednesday, November 25, when asked what initially led to Rodgers, 42, being benched as the starting quarterback ahead of the Steelers’ highly-anticipated Friday, November 27, matchup against the Denver Broncos.

McCarthy, who previously coached Rodgers during the quarterback’s time at the Green Bay Packers, explained, “We got to a point, we’d talked about some things, communication, things like that, and there was an ultimatum made [that was] clearly out of his job description. So it was my decision to bench him.”.

After having “private conversations” with Rodgers, he was informed that backup quarterback Mason Rudolph would be stepping in for Friday’s game.

Rodgers addressed the coach’s decision during an appearance on the The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, where he proceeded to claim that McCarthy is “unhealthy.”.

The four-time NFL MVP alleged that McCarthy had fallen asleep during team meetings, missed multiple team walkthroughs and was unwilling to connect with the team’s defensive players.

Rodgers also claimed that his longtime coach had yelled, “One, two, three, Packers!” when breaking a huddle during the Philadelphia Eagles game, hinting that McCarthy wasn’t aware of what team he was coaching at the time.

Sources indicate that “The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional,” McCarthy said in his Wednesday press conference, referring to Rodgers’ allegations against him. “There’s conversations prior to that. [It was an] embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments.”.

When asked why he was the right person to keep leading the Steelers, McCarthy replied, “I know how to win.”.

Shortly after Rodgers’ controversial interview, the Steelers confirmed they “released” the athlete while adding that he is no longer part of the organization.

McCarthy admitted on Wednesday that he was “disappointed” over Rodgers’ comments, but stated he was “proud” of the team’s leadership and “urgency” to move forward as a unit.

“Aaron and I have a long history,” he explained, speaking about what led to Rodgers’ firing. “He has a lot of opinions, and those are things we always talked about. Once again, I consider those private conversations.”.

McCarthy was fired from the Packers in 2018 after 12 years with the team for 12 years. Rodgers was the quarterback during his tenure, and they had their public ups and downs before McCarthy accepted the Steelers’ head coach job in 2026, where Rodgers had been playing since 2025.

When asked why he thought teaming back up with Rodgers for the 2026 Steelers season would be a good idea, McCarthy said, “We had a number of conversations early in the process of him returning.”.

McCarthy hinted that those talks went well, but something recently changed.

It has been revealed that in 2024, The Brat released a song about her insecurities around the world’s biggest pop star: “I couldn’t even be her if I tried,” she sings. “I’m opposite, I’m on the other side.”.

In 2025, The Star seemed to clap back to The Brat by releasing a song of her own about their relationship. In it, she accused The Brat of consuming illegal substances—which is fair enough.

In the time since The Brat released a song about The Star, The Exec says, The Star has “done this performance that she’s supportive of her...but she’s not.” In fact, says The Exec, artists who seem earmarked as The Star’s intentionally DO not collaborate professionally with her rivals, who also seem to be barred from taking part in her social world.

In 2023, The Protégé released a song that appeared to intimate a falling-out between her and a once-beloved mentor: “Trust that you betrayed, confusion that still lingers / Took everything I loved and crushed it in between your fingers.” But then, at the 2024 Grammys, The Star was seen vibing to The Protégé’s performance.

According to recent reports, before that was The California Girl—an adult pretending to be a child—and her feud with The Star, who might be a child pretending to be an adult. And, of course, the Kardashian affair, the details of which we are excluding from this narrative. (Yet another protégé, let’s call her The Blonde, remains in The Star’s good graces.).

“It’s truly Regina George,” The Exec notes.

There once lived a music critic who dared pan The Star. Around then, members of her friend group, one of whom she lived with, were getting courted by The Star. The Critic felt The Star was “ordering friends from a catalog.” After her negative review ran, The Critic’s friends—professional musicians all, who previously credited The Critic for their early success—shunned her. Her roommate, seemingly of her own accord, asked her to move out of their shared duplex. The Star had won.

A SIDE In a 2020 documentary about herself, The Star repeated a story she has often told about how a massive part of her feels frozen at 16, when she became famous. Though if she is frozen at 16, she has repeatedly—and mightily—fought against stasis. In her younger years, she avoided electoral politics, could not see how articulating her opinion was necessary. Later, she found her voice, making statements and endorsements for Democratic candidates, including Kamala Harris for president. She speaks in favor of LGBTQ+ rights, gun control, and making Juneteenth a national holiday. She becomes someone on whom nothing is lost.

Sources indicate that B SIDE You only become famous if you really, really want to. Lana Del Rey mentioned as much to the BBC in 2024. And The Star really, really did. “She wants it,” Del Rey said. “She’s told me so many times she wants it more than anyone.”.

Recent findings suggest that but if fame is a fickle food, as ­Emily Dickinson—The Star’s sixth cousin, according to Ancestry.com—observed, it is also impunity. You might end up like Barbra Streisand, cloning Coton de Tulears and building a mall in your basement. Or like Jim Carrey, watching YouTube videos all day from your estate in Maui. Or like whatever Elon Musk is doing right now.

Fame also fractures trust. A life grows and shrinks in inverse proportion to the size of its celebrity.

When they were close, The Person Familiar says, The Star’s professional life was run by a cabinet of three, including her mother, who acts as The Star’s manager; her longtime tour manager; and her publicist, to whom we only beg for mercy.

It has been revealed that “Nobody is beyond reproach with her,” claims The Person Familiar. Perhaps not even The Star’s sometimes close and dear friend who, after their private correspondence spilled across the tabloids as part of a public lawsuit, was not seen at The Star’s wedding. “If you don’t see it her way, she comes after you.”.

It has been revealed that “It’s always the same,” The Person Familiar says. “They say something she doesn’t like and they are dead to her. She’d be at dinner at [redacted]’s, then three weeks later, ‘Oh no, I hate her guts.’ ”.

A/B SIDE Okay, so The Star has a reputation for being punitive. She seems too invested in her own victimhood. Where might she have learned to be so?

Stars function, as cultural theorist Stuart Hall observed, as a mirror. “I want you to know / I’m a mirrorball,” The Star sang in a 2020 hit. “I’ll show you every version of yourself tonight.”.

Sources indicate that the Star holds up a mirror to us, and what the mirror states is this: If churches were once our society’s primary source of community, identity, and meaning, in these secular times we turn instead to celebrities. And we look, especially, to singers, because who among us is immune to music? The way a song can pitch you forward in space, sustain you through time; the way you swear some songs are written just for you.

A SIDE Stars, they’re just like us. Despite her life in perfect meter, lasting love had long eluded The Star. But it turned out she was a princess, this was a fairy tale, and we were in Hollywood. Her latest beau—regretfully we must call him Redwood—brought to her life a new form of intensity, a golden light, as they courted at a stadium show, a podcast interview, more shows, in Instagram posts. They have so much in common, The Star points out: They both perform at stadiums. He practices; she rehearses. He plays games, she plays shows.

Sources indicate that and all she had ever wanted from the world was that it celebrate her milky goodness, that her altruism not be mistaken for covert narcissism. Ahead of her wedding, the happy couple donates $26 million to local charities. Since then, The Star released four newly introduced songs, introduced an Oscar campaign, including performing at the Academy Museum Gala, and got a haircut.

B SIDE Summer 2026. The world’s most famous sexy baby—who insists that she is really a monster on a hill—chooses, as the site of her nuptials, midtown Manhattan during a heat wave. Her guests nibble on buffet food as thousands of Newly introduced Yorkers lose power.

Recent findings suggest that it is not lost on them that her $26 million giveaway, apart from being a tax write-off, is akin to a person making $81,228—the median household income in New York City—giving away $1,055. (In fall 2025, when this article was commissioned, The Star was worth $1.6 billion. By the time this issue goes to press, she will be worth over $2 billion, or the GDP of Eritrea.).

Industry observers note that “To become a billionaire,” The Star’s ex Matt Healy once told the Doomscroll podcast, “you don’t really care that much about culture.” He wasn’t speaking specifically about The Star but the deadening effects of modern wealth. Beyond need lies want. Beyond want, greed.

A/B SIDE And beyond greed was a tricked-out walled garden for the enchanted, her betrothed, and 1,000 of their family and friends, including, according to news reports, at least one government contractor who did not respond to multiple requests for comment. (In March his company took over our nation’s largest ICE detention facility. Earlier this year a father of three was pronounced dead there, after struggling with five guards, the second death at the camp in as many months. His name was Geraldo Lunas Campos.).

In other news, the wedding reportedly featured a raffle where a lucky guest won a Chanel bag. Another allegedly won a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle. Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. reportedly locked out its own security staff for the occasion, like it was a Mob bar—the kind with no windows. Not even members of the New York Police Department were allowed their own phones on site.

Love may be free, but the performance of it is not. It requires crates, trucks, officers on overtime, private jets, SUVs, HVACs, all the queen’s horses, all the queen’s men, a Jumbotron. Conspiracy theories do not tell you the truth, but they do tell a kind of psychological truth about a place or its people. Had The Star and Redwood filmed the ceremony, perhaps for theatrical release or streaming—maybe on Disney+, which paid The Star a king’s ransom for the rights to another project? (A person with knowledge says the couple has no looks to drop a documentary about their significant day.).

Around the barricades of Madison Square Garden, in the wake left by The Star, her groom, and their guests, her fans gathered. Some had been there for hours, wanting to be nearer to their pious majesty. A white truck passed. Pastries—from the merrymaking gentry presumably, though who can say for certain—were distributed, with an assist from a cop in uniform and gear.

If you listened carefully then to the sounds of the city—not for any semantic meaning, but if you were to really pitch your ears to the utopic promise of music—you might have heard the determined whoosh of a weighted blade dropping, dropping, dropping, the ax of public opinion falling in downward demotic motion.

Why Black Friday Is the Perfect Time to Start a Gym Membership

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (765 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that most people are probably waiting until Jan.
  • Sources indicate that the week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit.
  • According to recent reports, this week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a new air fryer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the fresh year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

Sources indicate that the week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on new tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

According to recent reports, this week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a new air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for upcoming Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

It has been revealed that deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

Try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

Be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

Recent findings suggest that gyms also run sales around Fresh Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

That's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're new. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

From Black Friday to Upcoming Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K strategy works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your New Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

This is also the season when many workplaces and health plans wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some looks include gym memberships or discounts.

HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before Latest Year's resolution time arrives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aaron Rodgers is one of the best-ever quarterbacks to play in the NFL, but it’s often his antics off the field that get the most people talking.

Rodgers — who was the Green Bay Packers superstar quarterback for 18 seasons before joining the New York Jets in 2023 and the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2025 — came under fire in November 2021 when it was revealed he misled people about his COVID-19 vaccination status when he told reporters that he was “immunized” when he hadn’t actually been vaccinated.

The athlete defended his use of the phrase, calling it “the truth.”.

“Had there been a follow-up to my statement that I’d been immunized, I would have responded with this: I would have said, ‘Look, I’m not some sort of anti-vax-flat-Earther. I’m somebody who’s a critical thinker,’” Rodgers later explained on the Pat McAfee Show. “I march to the beat of my own drum. I believe strongly in bodily autonomy, [in the] ability to make choices for your body, not to have to acquiesce to some woke culture or crazed group of individuals who say you have to do something.”.

He raised eyebrows again in November 2026, when his controversial comments about Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy amid his benching ended with the team releasing the quarterback hours later.

Keep scrolling for all of Rodgers’ controversies through the years:.

While a contestant on The Bachelorette in 2016, Aaron’s brother Jordan Rodgers told future wife JoJo Fletcher that he and Aaron “don’t really have that much of a relationship.”.

Sources indicate that “It’s just kind of the way he’s chosen to do life and I’ve chosen to stay close with my family and my parents and my brother,” Jordan explained at the time. “Yeah, it’s not ideal and I love him and I can’t imagine what it’s like to be in his shoes and have the pressure he has, the demands from people that he has. Don’t have hard feelings against him, it’s just how things go right now.”.

The brothers’ estrangement only grew worse as the years went on, particularly after both Jordan and other brother Luke Rodgers called out Aaron for allegedly not being there for their family amid the California wildfires in 2018. (Aaron also missed Jordan’s wedding in 2022.).

In Aaron’s 2024 Netflix docuseries, Aaron Rodgers: Enigma, he reflected on the strain Jordan’s Bachelorette stint put on their relationship.

Industry observers note that “It wasn’t like I was super duper close with everybody in the family. I was close with my little brother [Jordan],” Aaron mentioned. “But in actuality, it goes back to stuff from high school that kind of made me feel distant. Stuff in college, stuff post-college. I was quiet about it. I thought the best way to do it was just don’t talk about it publicly.”.

He recalled that Jordan — and the show producers — did the opposite of that by making it clear during hometowns that Aaron was absent. “And what do they do? They go on a bulls— show and leave two empty chairs,” Aaron stated. “They all agreed this was a good thing to do, to leave two empty chairs at a stupid dating show that my brother just went on to get famous — his words, not mine. That he ended up winning. But a dinner that was during the season, I was never asked to go to. Not that I would’ve gone.”.

According to recent reports, aaron also alleged in the December 2024 doc that he “found a lot of resistance” from his family when he stopped practicing the same Christian religion he was taught as a child. Instead, the athlete turned to “other religions and plant medicine” which fueled his “alternative lifestyle.” The religious shift “definitely changed the dynamics of my family,” he added.

In November 2026, Aaron and Jordan reunited and shared photo of their hangout. The pair’s reunion came after Aaron and Luke were spotted together on the sidelines at a Steelers game.

Aaron — who contracted COVID-19 in November 2021 — was forced to pay $14,650 for breaking NFL COVID-19 safety protocols as an unvaccinated player. His violations included attending a party with other teammates and speaking to reporters without a mask on. The Packers were fined $300,000 for not disciplining him or reporting his violations.

In August 2022, Aaron claimed on “The Aubrey Marcus Podcast” that doing ayahuasca helped him win two back-to-back MVP awards in 2020 and 2021.

“I don’t think it’s a coincidence. I really don’t. I don’t really believe in coincidences at this point,” he stated. “It’s the universe bringing things to happen when they’re supposed to happen and there’s signs and synchronicities all around us at all times if we’re awake enough to see them and to take them in and to listen to our intuition when it’s speaking to us or, you know, pounding us in the head saying, ‘Hey dummy, this is what you’re supposed to be doing.'”.

In November 2022, Packers backup QB DeShone Kizer claimed on “The Breneman Show” podcast that Aaron once encouraged him to question whether the September 11 attacks happened.

“He shut the door, and the first thing that comes out of Aaron Rodgers’ mouth was ‘Do you believe in 9/11?’” Kizer recalled, noting that Aaron wanted him to “‘read up on that’” and to “go back and look into some of the conspiracies around it.”.

It has been revealed that during multiple off-seasons, Aaron kept fans — and the Green Bay Packers — waiting for long periods of time while he publicly hinted at a possible desire to be traded or retire altogether. After ultimately sticking with the Packers every time, in 2023 he and the team finally pulled the trigger when Aaron was traded to the Jets.

Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen called out Aaron for allegedly cheating at the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am golf tournament in February 2023.

Recent findings suggest that “I love Aaron, but he did [cheat],” Allen noted on Barstool Sports’ “Pardon My Take” podcast in August 2023. Allen accused Aaron of “sandbagging,” meaning he downplayed how good he was at golf before the match in order to be afforded extra strokes during the match.

Sources indicate that “He may have gotten seven or eight strokes too many at Pebble Beach, or nine,” Allen claimed “other sources” said. Then he joked, “I think Aaron Rodgers should be in jail.”.

Jimmy Kimmel found himself in a years-long feud with Aaron after he poked fun at the NFL star’s controversial COVID-19 vaccine beliefs in 2021. “Nothing indicates I heal myself with crystals like this haircut — that little knot on top,” Kimmel said in a November 2021 Jimmy Kimmel Live! monologue before flashing to a selfie of Rodgers in a man bun. “Aaron is a Karen, that’s the fact of the matter.”.

It has been revealed that in March 2023, Aaron revealed on The Pat McAfee Show that he was interested in seeing the list of names that were connected to the late convicted sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein. Kimmel shared snippets of Aaron’s interview on his show and implied that he might have a potential head injury.

Aaron didn’t respond at the time, but he stoked the fire in January 2024 when he insinuated that Kimmel should be worried about the names on Epstein’s list coming out — implying that the comedian had some connection to the accused sex offender. “I’ll tell you what, if that list comes out, I will definitely be popping some sort of bottle,” Aaron said on The Pat McAfee Show.

Sources indicate that kimmel slammed Aaron via X for his remarks, denying any connection to Epstein. “Dear A——-: for the record, I’ve not met, flown with, visited, or had any contact whatsoever with Epstein, nor will you find my name on any ‘list’ other than the clearly-phony nonsense that soft-brained wackos like yourself can’t seem to distinguish from reality,” Kimmel wrote in January 2024. “Your reckless words put my family in danger. Keep it up and we will debate the facts further in court. @AaronRodgers12.”.

Industry observers note that after Kimmel went off on Aaron’s reckless accusations and actions on his talk show, the quarterback responded to the backlash. “I wish him the best. I don’t give a s— what he says about me,” Aaron mentioned on a January 2024 episode of The Pat McAfee Show. “As long as he understands what I actually said, that I’m not accusing him of being on a list. I’m all for moving forward.”.

It has been revealed that aaron raised eyebrows in September 2024 when he was caught pushing Jets coach Robert Saleh away when he came in for a hug during their game against the New England Patriots. The awkward moment caused some viewers to think there was tension between the player and coach.

“He’s not a substantial hugger usually,” Aaron said of Saleh in his postgame press conference, explaining, “So I didn’t know he was going for the hug. He likes to do the two-hand chest push.” He insisted the moment “wasn’t awkward at all,” which Saleh echoed himself.

In a recent development, the following month, amid the Jets disappointing start to the season, Saleh was fired. Rumors began to swirl that Aaron’s relationship with Saleh played into the franchise’s choice to let him go, which he denied. “As far as any of the ridiculous allegations out there, I’m not going to spend more than one sentence in response to it,” Aaron stated during an October 2024 appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. “I resent any of those accusations because they’re patently false.”.

During his first day at the Pittsburgh Steelers’ training camp in June 2025, Rodgers shared that he had gotten married “a couple months” earlier. The quarterback did not reveal the identity of his spouse. However, he revealed in December 2024 that he was dating a woman named Brittani.

According to recent reports, in November 2026, news broke that the Steelers were benching Aaron ahead of the team’s Thanksgiving week game against the Denver Broncos after back-to-back losses. Following the shocking decision, Aaron appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and aired his grievances with head coach McCarthy.

Aaron accused McCarthy of sleeping through meetings, missing a walkthrough and being “unhealthy.” He also claimed that McCarthy yelled, “One, two, three, Packers!” during a huddle break, hinting that he was unaware of which team he was actually coaching.

“We got to a point, we’d talked about some things, communication, things like that, and there was an ultimatum made [that was] clearly out of his job description,” McCarthy stated during a press conference. “So it was my decision to bench him.”.
