📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that netflix is always adding new movies to its already-large library, but the flip side is that each month, it also removes a bunch of familiar favorites. So, while you might prioritize the new Netflix additions, it's worth making time to watch some soon-to-depart movies while you still have the chance.

Industry observers note that on December 1, 2026, Netflix is set to remove 37 movies from its library. This includes my favorite movie of all time (and its equally five-star sequel), a beloved '80s coming-of-age story, and a very intense thriller that stars the late, great Patrick Stewart. And these are just some of the movies that are leaving.

In a recent development, that's a big number, which is why I've combed through the list and picked out a more manageable selection of five great movies you need to watch before they wave Netflix goodbye. Plus, I've also included the full list of movies being removed from Netflix on December 1, if you want to pick your own.

In the headline, I called “Alien” a “sci-fi masterpiece,” and if anything, that’s underplaying my love of this titan of the genre. It’s my favorite movie of all time, and it started my favorite media franchise. This 1979 horror introduced the world to the Xenomorph, and the terrifying alien creature has been a staple of pop culture since. Directed by Ridley Scott, and with a star-making turn from Sigourney Weaver, it’s more than worthy of its enduring legacy.

In a recent development, the premise is simple: a group of deep-space truckers is awoken from hypersleep when their ship alerts them to a strange transmission on a nearby planet. The source of the signal brings pure terror onboard, as they encounter a lethal predator, perfectly formed to kill. The almost-as-good sequel, “Aliens,” is also leaving Netflix on Dec. 1, so make sure you stream them both quickly. Trust me, they make for the perfect sci-fi double-bill.

Watch "Alien" on Netflix until December 1.

Sources indicate that the entertainment world mourned the great Patrick Stewart last month, so it feels like a fitting time to recommend “Green Room.” This thriller is noteworthy because Stewart plays against type. He’s not playing a hero or a warm father figure, but instead the veteran actor plays the leader of a neo-Nazi group. And he’s chilling! The movie was also the final film released in Anton Yelchin’s lifetime. The actor tragically passed away in 2016, at just 27.

Sources indicate that in “Green Room,” members of a scrappy punk band are booked to play a dive bar, which they soon discover is actually a clubhouse for a neo-Nazi group. After witnessing a member of the group commit murder, they are trapped in the green room backstage and have to fight their way out. Also starring Imogen Poots and Callum Turner, “Green Room” is fast-paced and very loud, not to mention splattered with fake blood. It’s a hoot, and seriously intense.

Watch "Green Room" on Netflix until December 1.

Netflix is removing “The Karate Kid”, its two original sequels released in 1986 and 1989, and the 2010 remake soon. I have a soft spot for the remake (please, flame me in the comments!), but I can’t deny that the 1984 original is the true classic in the bunch. One of the most iconic and beloved coming-of-age movies of all time, this flick is charming, relatable, and very good fun.

It has been revealed that daniel LaRusso (Ralph Macchio) moves from Latest Jersey to Los Angeles, California, and finds the transition tough. Things only get worse when he’s harassed by the students of the Cobra Kai dojo, led by Johnny Lawrence (William Zabka). But Daniel learns to stand up for himself when his apartment's handyman, Mr. Miyagi (Pat Morita), takes him under his wing and teaches him karate. This gives Daniel confidence and a new perspective.

Watch "The Karate Kid" on Netflix until December 1.

Recent findings suggest that meg Ryan and Tom Hanks are a classic romantic-comedy pairing, having starred in “Joe Versus the Volcano,” “You’ve Got Mail” and “Sleepless in Seattle.” Each flick sees them playing characters who fall in love across the movie’s runtime. It’s 1993’s “Sleepless in Seattle” that’s waving goodbye to Netflix next week, but make sure to give it a watch before then if you want a charming rom-com. Yes, it’s sappy, but I dare you not to get emotional.

It has been revealed that architect Sam Baldwin (Hanks) moves from Chicago to Seattle with his eight-year-old son, Jonah (Ross Malinger), after the death of his wife. Aware his father is struggling to come to terms with the loss, Jonah calls a national radio station to find his dad a new wife. Listening in is Annie Reed (Ryan), a Baltimore reporter, who falls for Sam, despite being engaged. It’s a very 1990s plot for a movie; these days, Jonah would have probably just posted a TikTok.

Watch "Sleepless in Seattle" on Netflix until December 1.

Jessica Chastain recently starred in the Netflix Original thriller “Heartland,” which, according to many critics (including TG’s Alix Blackburn), is a bit of a misfire. However, one Chastain-led movie that does hit the mark is “Zero Dark Thirty,” a sprawling political thriller from director Kathryn Bigelow, which was nominated for a clutch of Oscars including Best Picture. Its chunky 157-minute runtime might put some viewers off, but give the film your full attention, and you’ll be richly rewarded with a gripping war movie.

Chastain plays Maya Krauser, a fictional CIA intelligence analyst, with a singular focus. Her mission is to find terrorist leader Osama bin Laden, and her determination borders on and then crosses over into obsession. Set over multiple years, “Zero Dark Thirty” chronicles the decade-long manhunt for the man responsible for the world-altering September 11 attacks.

Watch "Zero Dark Thirty" on Netflix until December 1.

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • Industry observers note that you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

Industry observers note that you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting latest movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

In a recent development, chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

Sources indicate that go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Sources indicate that pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Industry observers note that get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

In a recent development, hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Industry observers note that volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

It has been revealed that shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should blueprint ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you initiative to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most notable advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

Industry observers note that it’s the Thanksgiving holiday weekend. Millions of people will soon be gathering with family, catching everybody up on the goings-on in their lives over the past year. A subset of those people will be gamers, who may be subject to blank stares from aunts and uncles whose conception of the multibillion-dollar industry has not progressed beyond calling every console a “Nintendo” or confused inquiries from relatives who’ve just recently been made aware that video games are a thing by all the breathless coverage of GTA 6 on network television.

Both of those people are my mom.

She has never really taken an interest in what I do, and while that stings a bit, she is at least happy that I am happy in my chosen profession and that’s good enough for me.

In one of the exceedingly rare times that she has ever asked me directly about my job, she called me the other day asking if I was “excited” for the pending release of GTA 6. She used stronger language than “excited” but I’m not gonna repeat exactly what she said to me because it’s something no child should ever hear their parent say to them in any context but it involved “cream” and “drawers” so draw your own conclusions.

Sources indicate that I explained to her that 1) ew and 2) I’m not excited per se, but I am interested to see what happens with this game and how we talk about it. But I also told her that despite the sensational coverage of the game, its development price tag, and its status as the most anticipated game this decade…it’s not for me. I’ve never been into those games and I don’t see GTA 6 changing that stance much. We rapidly moved on to other topics.

Industry observers note that at first, this exchange reopened that unhealed wound of “I wish you took a greater interest in the thing I’ve built a life on.” If she had, she might know that I’m more of a Kingdom Hearts girlie, the game I used to play by ferrying my PS2 from its box under my bed to the 12-inch tube TV in her room when I was 16 years old. But as I think about it now, even though she’s wildly missed the mark on my tastes and preferences, I actually really appreciate that she asked at all. She saw a video game on TV and thought, “Oh hey, my daughter does video games, let me talk to her about that.” That was her attempt at connecting with me, and it’s way more than a lot of other parents do when it comes to engaging with their children’s passion professions, so thanks, mom.

Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1907 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch.
  • Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
  • When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”.

When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she states.

In a recent development, dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

The casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He notes to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”.

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most key roles, including the exciting newly introduced additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

Sources indicate that in Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy demonstrated me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” claims Maisler.

Sources indicate that there was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she says. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”.

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” states Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”.

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” claims Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”.

In a recent development, when Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the significant surprises in the ensemble.”.

Sources indicate that taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” indicates Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”.

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” indicates Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”.

Sources indicate that pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”.

Industry observers note that the third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” says Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

It has been revealed that for Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she notes. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most notable for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

Recent findings suggest that “Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 demonstrates a upcoming confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

Sources indicate that the dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

It has been revealed that wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

Industry observers note that “It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”.

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Recent findings suggest that as Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley claims. “There’s a significant difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As we get older, things change, and while I don't necessarily recommend that someone swap their entire routine just because of a number, there are certain factors to consider, especially as you pass the 40 mark.
  • This applies to both men and women, but particularly women, whose hormones change with perimenopause and menopause, which impacts lean muscle mass and joint and bone health.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As we get older, things change, and while I don't necessarily recommend that someone swap their entire routine just because of a number, there are certain factors to consider, especially as you pass the 40 mark.

This applies to both men and women, but particularly women, whose hormones change with perimenopause and menopause, which impacts lean muscle mass and joint and bone health. But regardless, sarcopenia (the age-related, progressive loss of muscle mass, strength, and physical function) begins to accelerate through the 40s and 50s and still applies to everyone.

For that reason, there are a few tweaks we can make to help the transition, and I'm going to lay them out for you below using my experience as a personal trainer and fitness editor.

Industry observers note that I absolutely refuse to change someone's gym program just because of a number. Instead, I listen to the client and their goals, potential health conditions, injuries, or life experiences, and I also program to my clients' abilities and scale accordingly.

In fact, I train my 72-year-old dad like he's 30 years younger and he's stronger and more mobile than ever.

That noted, people over 40 may notice slower recovery times and changes to joint mobility, strength, or muscle mass. This is a period of time when I think building and maintaining muscle becomes extremely important for function, balance and performance.

For some, it may be possible to remain doing high-impact cardio or HIIT routines, but for many, I see a gradual shift toward low-impact routines such as Pilates or yoga and strength training, which may involve lifting weights at home or in the gym.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Changes to hormones and lower collagen levels mean muscles may take slightly longer to repair and recover from workouts, which makes overtraining easier to accidentally fall into.

Lower collagen levels can also impact your joints, which play a vital role in mobility; tendons and ligaments will also lose elasticity with age, which means you'll need to really focus on proper warm-ups and cool-downs to maintain range of motion without injury or strain.

Alongside sarcopenia, which I mentioned earlier, bone density decreases into your 40s and 50s as well, impacting balance and strength, which can make the likelihood of injuries or falls higher.

Recent findings suggest that sam Hopes is a level 3 qualified trainer, a level 2 Reiki practitioner and fitness editor at Tom's Guide. She is also currently undertaking her Yoga For Athletes training course.

Sam has written for various fitness brands and websites over the years and has experience across brands at Future, such as Live Science, Fit&Well, Coach, and T3.

Having coached at fitness studios like F45 and Virgin Active and taken on both 1:1 and group, Sam now primarily teaches outdoor bootcamps, bodyweight, and kettlebells.

She also coaches mobility and flexibility classes several times a week.

Sam has completed two mixed doubles Hyrox competitions in London and the Netherlands and finished her first doubles attempt in 1:11.

BigfootControlControl ResonantCreepy.

It has been revealed that one of my favorite video games is Control. I also like this year’s Control Resonant, but not quite as much. And one of the best parts of those games is the government reports and files documenting creepy happenings and events in the game’s universe. Meanwhile, here in real life, the United States Forest Service has recently released some files about Bigfoot, and I was very pleased to see that feel like they fell right out of Control.

Sources indicate that as reported by The New York Times, last month the USFS published a few documents and reports related to Bigfoot as part of a Freedom of Information request. One file is just a clipping of a newspaper article from a Montana newspaper in the ’80s about big, strange footprints found in the snow. The other two are far more interesting.

Industry observers note that first, a 1982 report written by someone who was sent out to study alleged Bigfoot tracks found in Mill Creek, Oregon. Look at this and tell me it doesn’t look and read like something you’d pick up in Control.

Sources indicate that the report goes over, in a lot of detail, the footprints that were spotted. Ultimately, the report’s conclusion was that these tracks were fake, with the writer citing inconsistencies with gait pattern, signs of tampering with leaves, and other pieces of evidence that led them to conclude the tracks were “made by something other than a 300-pound plus two-footed being.”.

The other piece of Bigfoot documentation released by the USFS is what appears to be a short document written by someone who really thought Petty Creek, Montana was special and historically important. One reason it was historically important: Bigfoot, baby. Here’s the bit about a Bigfoot sighting that allegedly happened in the ’40s.

Sources indicate that another type creature that walked on its hind legs, that altho there wasn’t actual sightings, tracks, a strong odor, and a grunting sound were observed. The first time was when four of us went in to pack out a six point bull elk on our backs and on arriving where the elk was supposed to be laying we found the intrails only and in the snow coming to and leading away from the area was a large set of tracks. At first we guessed it was a very large bear except bears don’t walk on their hind legs only for short distances and ordinarily would drag a carcass this large.

Sources indicate that this event took place in 1949 in the South fork of Petty cr. about where the present Garden point road goes. The following year when W.W. Schmitz was hunting in the upper Bills creek area he came across the same type of tracks and smelled a strong odor and heard a grunting type noise. He decided that he could find elk elsewhere and left the area. At this time we had never heard of Bigfoot so passed it off as something we didn’t want anything to do with and let it go at that.

The whole thing was typed up on a typewriter and even contains a bit of extra text at the bottom, written afterwards by hand. All of this, including the official seals, the black-and-white photos, and the matter-of-fact writing in the official report, feels like stuff I’d read in Control right before encountering Bigfoot. Sadly, it’s unlikely a big ape stalks the woods of the United States. But it’s fun to read about it, you know?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one of Star Trek's most iconic fight scenes was also one of the most miserable to film. William Shatner recently talked about how bad it was to do the Gorn fight in the original series, and how it felt even worse to actually shoot than it looked onscreen.

"Arena" is likely one of the most memorable episodes of Star Trek decades later. Unfortunately, that's not necessarily a great thing, as it contains (in my opinion) an obscenely bad fight scene. It's one in which Shatner's Kirk fights in slow motion with a member of the Gorn species. In addition to the iconic scene aging poorly, with effects that even looked dated back then, Shatner mentioned at New York Comic Con it was also terrible to film (via Reddit):.

The guy was in this rubber suit; it's 120 degrees in the desert. I have to roll in the regolith and get all dusty. And when you go to brush it off, you get blood.

The "regolith," which by the way are the minerals that settle on top of bedrock, were so abrasive that it made the fight very difficult to film. I'm sure most Star Trek fans don't need to rewatch the scene with a Paramount+ subscription to know the end result ultimately wasn't worth the pain and toil. Still, lame fight aside, "Arena" is a pretty compelling episode.

I Just Found Out Wil Wheaton Apologized To Patrick Stewart After TNG, But I'm Not Surprised By The Captain's Response.

Sources indicate that "Arena" starts when Kirk and the Gorn are transported to the planet to battle thanks to a third species named the Metrons. The Metrons wish to see a fight to the death, but are impressed when Kirk outmaneuvers the Gorn and spares its life instead. Both are then returned to their ship, with the lesson being that brains can overcome brawn with some quick thinking and skills.

Sources indicate that it's great to hear William Shatner talk about the sillier times, as Star Trek fans were hit with some heavy news as of late. The passing of Walter Koenig was a gut punch to many, and following it with Patrick Stewart's death had many Trekkies out of the count. Shatner has even joked he's keeping an eye out for the Grim Reaper, trying to take the edge off such a heavy time.

According to recent reports, as for Star Trek in general, there's an overarching question about what direction the franchise is headed after its 60th anniversary. There's a movie in development, but with no solid timeline and no word that there are any reveals actively being made, there are a lot of questions that still need to be answered.

In a recent development, for the time being, there's a lot of Star Trek to watch and enjoy over on Paramount+. Those who have never seen "Arena can go and check it out now for the first time, or some of the other classic Trek highlights as we wait for newly introduced entries in the franchise.

10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests.
  • If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely fresh side of the game.

If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

Sources indicate that EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

Recent findings suggest that when you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

While driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Industry observers note that stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Duran Duran has revealed the death of its iconic guitarist Andy Taylor “following a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer.” He was 65.

“Andy passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by family, on Monday 23rd November,” the “Hungry Like the Wolf” band declared in a Wednesday, November 25, statement.

Andy became one of the classic “Fab Five” members of Duran Duran when he joined the New Wave band in 1980, along with singer Simon Le Bon, keyboardist Nick Rhodes, drummer Roger Taylor and bassist John Taylor. (Andy, Roger, 66, and John, 66, were not related.).

The group went on to sell more than 100 million records worldwide and received a coveted star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1993. They were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022. (Andy left Duran Duran originally in 1986 but later returned for a five-year reunion stint between 2001 to 2006.).

Andy was also part of the 1980s supergroup the Power Station, along with Duran Duran bandmate John, Chic drummer Tony Thompson and frontman Robert Palmer. Formed in 1984, the Power Station scored U.S. Top 10 hits with “Some Like It Hot” and a cover for T. Rex’s “Get It On.”.

Le Bon, 68, declared during Duran Duran’s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony in 2022 that Andy was unable to attend after being diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.

It has been revealed that “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story,” Duran Duran noted on Wednesday. “From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”.

Industry observers note that the guitarist tied the knot with wife Tracey Wilson on the Sunset Strip in 1982 and they remained married until his death. They welcomed four children: Georgina, Isabella, Bethany, and Andrew.

“To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather. He was the rock of our family,” Tracey noted in a Monday statement. “For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home.”.

She continued, “Andy faced the last few years with so much courage and determination. He never gave up, fighting until the very end, never losing his love of life. The kindness and support shown to him by fans from all over the world throughout his illness brought him immense comfort and strength, and for that we will always be grateful. Andy knew just how deeply he was loved, and we take great comfort in that. We will miss him every single day.”.

Andy’s Duran Duran bandmates each paid tribute to the late musician with individual and heartfelt statements, with Le Bon fondly highlighting the “blond bombshell, firebrand teenager” he met in 1980.

“There’s a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart,” he wrote. “It’ll never close up; I won’t let it. I will miss him & love him for all my days.”.

John focused on Andy’s musicianship, describing him as a “demon” and a “killer riff-merchant, melodist, six string textualist.”.

Recent findings suggest that “[Andy] never ever left us, he was always there in the shadows, keeping an eye out, keeping it real,” the bassist noted. “And he will continue to be there, we will keep him close.”.

Rhodes, 64, hailed Andy’s guitar playing for being “sharp as a razor and blunt as a stone,” adding that his late bandmate was always “out on the edge, with a clear view.”.

“The incredible, talented musician and gifted songsmith arrived on a train from Cullercoats to knock us into shape and help us grow into the burgeoning version of Duran Duran that took on the world within a year or two of his arrival,” Roger added. “The sadness cuts extremely deep, but admiration and respect run even deeper for the Taylor that wasn’t related but will forever be my brother.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

One thing that keeps striking me about Grand Theft Auto 6 is how good the writing is, even compared to that in previous games in the series. I enjoyed those earlier games, sure, but the dialogue and storytelling in GTA 6 are a cut above the rest in terms of both the game’s compelling characters and its worldbuilding. The fact that GTAÂ is set in an analogue of the real world helps the worldbuilding bridge gaps that most fictional universes couldnât, but Iâm increasingly finding that the standout writing is fighting a war within the game itself against some of the other jokes that have been building up in the series for over a quarter century.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto, for obvious reasons, canât use the existing brand names that we see every day in real life. In this sense it’s the opposite of the Like a Dragon series, which proudly wears all its licensed brand deals on its chest and even had to write a narrative around losing the license to a key landmark in the seventh game in the series. Talking Budweiser into lending their brand name to GTA 4 would have been an uphill battle and maybe also raised some uncomfortable questions about the gameâs proximity to real-world places and events. Better to just call your in-game equivalent Pisswasser and move on.

It has been revealed that but weâre in 2026 now. The writing in theÂ GTA games has elevated and, to Rockstarâs credit, so have the fake brand names in general. Taco Bomb is a pretty good one as a stand-in for Taco Bell. ZIP for GAP is also good. Weazel News for Fox News makes sense on a couple of different levels, Snapmatic for Instagram is something that you recognize immediately upon hearing it. But there are a handful of brand names I think the series needs to ditch, as theyâre taking away from the more interesting narratives Rockstar wants to tell.

In a recent development, pisswasser is not a bad joke on its own, but it wears its welcome out fast. Marbles, the McDonaldâs stand-in in GTA, sells a burger called Substantial Balls. I get it, Big Mac, Big Balls, sure. But come on, man. Weâre scraping the bottom of the barrel here. Zombix isnât even a good pun. Itâs like someone filed that one in the ten minutes before the deadline. We need to start thinking intelligently about which of these benefit worldbuilding and which detract from it.

I’m not saying all of these need to go or even a majority of them. There are plenty of good joke brand names, but there are also ones that are very, very 2000s, and it would be better for the games if they disappear. Grand Theft Auto has grown with its audience, and it’s now delivering narratives that genuinely keep up with well-written modern movies, so why are we limiting aspects of it to jokes that would appear in an Epic Movie parody?

Rockstar can and should start taking a look at these and see what makes sense for their games every so often. Audit the world, donât just assume that because it existed in previous games, it needs to exist forever.

In a recent development, itâs not like brands donât just disappear from the real world all the time. Joannâs Fabrics isnât around anymore, but your world keeps spinning, just like it would if the Obey car line simply did not appear in a new game. You planning to take a Spirit Airlines flight this holiday? Youâre sure as hell not, nor would you be a sobbing mess on the floor if a Substantial Balls sandwich billboard wasnât overlooking a highway chase.

Sources indicate that there are already so many good jokes in these games that the lame ones can get cut out without losing anything. No one is wrong for liking them, but maybe the games themselves can be better for examining what works and what doesnât. No series has ever escaped a need for refreshing itself and iterating over the years and, in almost every way, GTA 6 nails it. Thereâs just one more thing I want to see them look at before they build their next GTA world, asking themselves if each jokey brand name still fits their vision. If it does, great! If they decide it would be better to snip, that would be fine, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've lost count of how many times I've settled down to play a brand-new game on Steam, only to be smacked in the face with a giant popup telling me to "Grab a controller and kick back!" instead of using my humble mouse and keyboard.

Industry observers note that thankfully for me I live in a multi-platform household, meaning a controller is never far out of reach. But I've also got staunch PC pals without a pad to pick up and who, rightly enough, don't want to fork out the kinda cash that PlayStation's DualSense or the Xbox controller require.

But I'm a firm believer that a good controller is a must-have tool in a PC gamer's repertoire these days, and we needn't immediately seek out the significant names when it comes to a comfortable, robust gamepad. Tons of budget-friendly options have popped up on the market over the years, and while some of them are admittedly pretty naff there are also a bunch of great controllers that won't break the bank.

Sources indicate that in fact, I've got three of 'em for under $25 for you right here. That's a third of the price of a DualSense controller! While they don't come with fancy haptics and adaptive triggers, they do offer stick-drift resistant, low-latency gaming. Which, as fun as the bells as whistles can be, are really the most key bits.

According to recent reports, A new and improved version of the original Nova Lite, the Nova Lite 2 has Hall effect everything, 1000 Hz polling, and trigger locks. It even has a mechanical D-pad, which is absurd for the money, really.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.

Price check: Amazon $29.99 (Grey).

Out of the three choices, our pad professional James Bentley tells me he likes the GameSir Nova Lite 2 the best, currently going for $23 at Walmart. It boasts comfort, decent polling, and Hall effect—so much better protection against that pesky stick drift. It's also got our highest review score out of the bunch thanks to its affordability, mechanical d-pad, and choice of 2.4Ghz and Bluetooth.

Recent findings suggest that it's not got great grip, however, and its budget is felt in the less-than-stellar plastic and rather simple software. But for the price you're paying? It's a great, basic choice for those who only need to reach for a controller occasionally.

We've already raved about Hall effect joysticks and how they spell the end for the dreaded stick drift. In this wireless gaming controller, they're a welcome feature, but this handful of gaming hardware packs a few quirky surprises too. For instance, there are extra bumper buttons.

Key specs: Hall effect sticks, triggers | 2.4G wireless | 19 h battery.

Price check: Best Buy $21.99 (Black) | Walmart $29.99 (Purple).

But if you're someone who's accustomed to the likes of the Switch Pro controller, you might find the 8BitDo Ultimate 2C a better fit, currently going for $20 at Amazon. It's got a pretty similar shape, and also sports those beloved Hall effect joysticks. It does have a little bit of a mushy d-pad but hey, look at that lovely colourway!

Finally, if you're looking to spend as little as possible, the GameSir Nova Lite comes in as the cheapest option at a mere $18. It's got less mappable buttons than its successor thanks to no back paddles, and is overall a downgrade. For the extra four bucks I'd personally just go for the newer version, but if you're really looking to really squeeze every cent, it's certainly an option worth considering.

It's incredible to think you can spend so little and get a stick drift-resistant wireless controller that doesn't completely suck. Luckily for the GameSir Nova Lite, it does all of the above and manages to feel good and light in the hands, too.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (410 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

AI May Be Scanning Your Private Signal Chats

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (410 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads.
  • In a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy.
  • Signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

In a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy. Systems-level capabilities like Gemini Intelligence (on Android) and Siri AI's Onscreen Awareness (on iOS and macOS) scan your screen and may be able to capture data from Signal conversations in the process, which can then be used to perform tasks. Not only does this potentially expose your information, but that of other conversation participants as well. Whitaker notes that this leaves privacy protections outside of Signal's control because the platform cannot easily restrict AI access to the app.

Signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

Sources indicate that the main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

People on iOS 27 can confirm or manually disable screenshot protection via Settings > Privacy > Block Siri AI. The compromise with this setting is that it also blocks you from taking screenshots of Signal conversations in the app and App Switcher, though you can disable it temporarily for 10 minutes if needed. On Android, Signal automatically engages the "Screen security" setting when it detects an AI agent attempting to access the screen. This, too, blocks screenshots inside the app and can be disabled via Settings > Privacy > App security > Screen security. Signal cannot block screenshots on macOS 27. However, users can add Signal to their Excluded Apps list via System Settings > Siri, which at least limits proactive access to conversations by Siri AI.

Tech Report: Claude just got a major update that lets you build your own desktop apps — no coding required

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that imagine creating your own budgeting app, meal planner or productivity tool by just describing what you want.
  • That's exactly what Anthropic is making possible with its latest Claude update.
  • Perhaps the best part is that you don't need a paid Claude subscription or any coding experience to get started.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that imagine creating your own budgeting app, meal planner or productivity tool by just describing what you want. Now imagine opening that app directly from your computer without digging through your chat history.

That's exactly what Anthropic is making possible with its latest Claude update. The company announced on Tuesday that consumers can now turn Claude Artifacts into desktop apps for Mac and Windows, complete with their own icons, dedicated windows, and notifications.

Perhaps the best part is that you don't need a paid Claude subscription or any coding experience to get started.

The feature is currently rolling out in beta across all Claude plans, including the free tier. And while AI chatbots have been able to build interactive tools for some time, this revision makes those creations considerably more practical for everyday use.

Until now, one of the drawbacks of building an interactive tool with Claude was that using it meant going back into Claude. Giving those creations a permanent place on your desktop changes that experience.

You could create a custom app that helps you stay focused throughout the workday, a family chore tracker or even a holiday shopping organizer that keeps tabs on your budget.

Here are five app ideas and prompts worth trying:.

Anthropic employees have already used the feature to create everything from a layered image editor to a computer performance monitor.

Apps can also work with services you've connected to Claude, opening up possibilities for more personalized tools.

Getting started doesn't require downloading a separate coding tool or setting up an API key.

Download or enhancement the Claude desktop app for Mac or Windows.

Describe the app you want Claude to build.

Try out the resulting Artifact and ask Claude to make any necessary changes.

Open the Share menu and select Install as app.

Review and confirm any requested permissions.

You can continue refining your creation through Claude, and changes to the original Artifact will carry over to the installed app.

In a recent development, there are several limitations to keep in mind. These apps aren't completely independent of Claude. You'll need an internet connection and an active Claude login to open them, and any AI requests they make count toward your existing usage limits.

Not every Artifact can be installed, either. Claude's standard documents, presentations and spreadsheets are among the exclusions.

According to recent reports, security is another consideration. Anthropic doesn't review apps before installation, and certain permissions can let an app modify or delete files on your computer.

Recent findings suggest that I'd recommend sticking with the default permissions unless your app genuinely needs additional access. Be especially careful about installing creations shared by others.

Industry observers note that prince William is reportedly actively considering a initiative for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”.

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is stated to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”.

It has been revealed that by implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Recent findings suggest that under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his strategy. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”.

Recent findings suggest that kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”.

#132651. Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1458 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if you or someone on your shopping list wants a new smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from.
  • Sources indicate that luckily, you do have options.
  • Contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you or someone on your shopping list wants a new smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

Sources indicate that luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own firm, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

Recent findings suggest that the Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

Recent findings suggest that where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

It has been revealed that you also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

For an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

As a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET notes Android users can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

Based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

While the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android people, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

Industry observers note that the Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

In a recent development, in CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?).

CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.).

In CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

Still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another company drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.
